W1_I1:
The wind chimes at the door rang as you burst through.

"I'm home——!"

Before Bae Ju-hyeon could even look up, you dove straight into her arms, scattering petals from her apron.

"Slow down." That's what she said, but she instinctively held you close, her fingers gently fixing your messed-up hair.

"I got praised at school today! The teacher said I'm great at bringing energy!" You looked up, eyes shining bright.

Shon Seung-wan laughed: "That's just how you are."

She walked over and naturally took your backpack. "First set it down, you can tell me the whole story in a bit."

But you were already rapid-firing the day's events, stopping halfway through: "...But there was one classmate who seemed down today."

The flower shop went still for a moment.

Ju-hyeon set down the bouquet she'd just finished and quietly asked: "So what did you do?"

You thought for a second, a little embarrassed: "I just sat with her for a while."

Seung-wan smiled and gently touched your head: "That was enough."

When closing up, Ju-hyeon tucked a small branch into your hand.

"You did great today too."

On the way home, Seung-wan kept cracking jokes while you walked and looked back at the flowers.

You suddenly felt like the world was actually really gentle.

Bae Ju-hyeon looked up at you, said nothing for a moment, just turned down the TV volume a bit and patted the spot next to her.

"Sit down. Take your time."

You stood still and started recapping everything—who said what first, how you responded, how it escalated—speaking so fast like you were still in the middle of it.

"Anyway, I wasn't wrong." That was your final statement.

She listened, then nodded gently, neither arguing nor agreeing.

"So what matters to you more right now?" she asked. "The rightness, or the relationship?"

You froze.

Shon Seung-wan handed you a glass of water and said with a smile: "You didn't back down right there, which already makes you pretty incredible."

Ju-hyeon reached over and straightened your slightly crooked collar, her tone still calm:

"If you want to end this, go make it clear; if you just want to win, you've already won halfway."

She paused, then added:

"But either way, I'm on your side."

You looked at the cup in your hands, and your emotions slowly settled.

Before you left the next morning, Seung-wan gently tapped you at the door: "Go. Direct player."

When you nodded, you had a bit more confidence than before.

Ju-hyeon nodded gently, her hand staying on your shoulder.
